items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: Because he liked me and he was very interested in me, like my second father. He took good care of me. He taught me a lot of music, too.

ctx.x: What musicians did you work with?

I worked with Buddy Petit, Chris Kelly. I worked with Manuel Perez. I had an opportunity to work with him. And I worked with Piron. Another fantastic trumpet man that nobody don't hear anything about is Amos White, and he's a professor at Berklee College of Music -- in music, a very fantastic man. He taught me a lot. And we had a band together and he took me around, and all these supposed to be big-time clarinetists like Picou, he showed me where they wasn't nothing. He did, too. Because he liked me and he was…
I had a wonderful time, but I left. I was known as the "Slap Tongue King."
